blocked.busy: Wait for the current Proton VPN action to finish.
blocked.checking: Wait for Proton VPN status before making changes.
blocked.cliMissing: Install the Proton VPN CLI before making changes.
blocked.connect: Proton VPN is not ready to connect.
blocked.disconnect: Proton VPN is not ready to disconnect.
blocked.guiConflict: Close the Proton VPN desktop app before making changes.
blocked.other: Proton VPN is not ready for changes.
blocked.settings: Proton VPN is not ready for settings changes.
blocked.signedOut: Sign in to Proton VPN from a terminal before making changes.
blocked.stale: Refresh Proton VPN status before making changes. The last result may be outdated.
cli.checkFailed: Could not reach the Arch mirrors.
cli.checkTip: Asks your Arch mirrors with checkupdates. Nothing else reaches the network.
cli.updateTip: Opens Omarchy's system update in a terminal. It updates every package, the Proton VPN CLI included.
compat.unknown: Could not identify the Proton VPN CLI version. Core controls remain available.
compat.untested: Proton VPN CLI %1 is outside the tested %2–%3 range.
config.incompatible: Proton VPN configuration output is incompatible with this plugin.
config.readFailed: Could not read Proton VPN settings.
config.restartNotice: Establish a new VPN connection for this change to take effect.
connect.needCountryForCity: Choose a country before listing cities.
connect.serverFilters: A specific server ID cannot be combined with other connection filters.
connect.switchTip: Reconnect with these choices. Proton replaces the current connection.
degraded.cliMissing: The official Proton VPN CLI is not installed or is not on PATH.
degraded.error: Proton VPN could not complete the last command. This can be a plugin, CLI, daemon, or keyring problem.
degraded.guiConflict: Proton VPN's desktop app is running. The official CLI refuses to operate until that app is closed.
degraded.signedOut: The CLI is installed but this session is signed out. Sign in from a terminal; this plugin never asks for a password or 2FA code.
degraded.stale: The last status probe failed. The previous result is still shown and may be outdated. Connection and settings changes stay disabled until a fresh probe succeeds.
discovery.noCities: No cities returned for that country.
dns.empty: Enter at least one DNS server IP.
dns.invalid: Invalid DNS address '%1'. Use IPv4 or IPv6.
failure.connectionTimeout: Proton VPN timed out while connecting. The CLI reached a server but the handshake did not finish.
failure.daemon: The Proton VPN daemon did not respond.
failure.empty: No matching Proton VPN servers were found.
failure.keyring: Proton VPN could not read saved credentials from the system keyring.
failure.network: Proton VPN could not reach the network.
failure.plan: This option is not available on the current plan.
failure.timeout: Proton VPN did not respond in time.
field.city.tooltip: Choose a city in that country. Multi-word names work.
field.country.tooltip: Use a country code such as US, or the full country name.
field.server.tooltip: Enter a server ID such as CH#242.
fix.cliMissing: Choose Install Proton VPN CLI. Omarchy installs the %1 package from Arch extra in a terminal, which asks for your password there. Proton's upstream Linux support list does not currently include Arch, so updates and support may be limited.
fix.connectionTimeout: The CLI reached Proton but the connection handshake timed out. Retry, or check the network. This is not a widget command-queue failure.
fix.daemon: Check that proton-vpn-daemon is running, then refresh. This is a Proton CLI/service problem.
fix.guiConflict: Quit the Proton VPN desktop application, then refresh this panel.
fix.keyring: Unlock or restart the system keyring (Secret Service), then refresh. This is a local session problem, not a widget parser bug.
fix.network: Check local network connectivity, then refresh. A failed probe is not treated as disconnected.
fix.signedOut: Choose Sign in to enter your username, password, and 2FA in a terminal, or run `%1` yourself. The panel refreshes once you are signed in.
fix.stale: Use Refresh after the network, daemon, or CLI is available again. Confirm `protonvpn status` in a terminal if the widget still fails.
fix.timeout: The Proton VPN command did not finish in time. Refresh after the CLI or daemon responds again.
health.stalled: Connected, but nothing has come back through the tunnel for 30 seconds. The server or the network under it may be down; reconnect or switch servers if it lasts.
ipc.badTarget: Use a country code (NL), a server ID (CH#242), a country and city (US New York), p2p, securecore, or tor with an optional country code, or random or fastest alone.
killSwitch.blocking: The VPN dropped and Kill Switch is blocking internet traffic, so nothing leaks. Connect again to restore access, or set Kill Switch to Off.
killSwitch.confirm: This briefly drops the VPN, sets Kill Switch to %1, then reconnects to %2.
killSwitch.interrupted: Kill Switch change interrupted and the VPN is disconnected: %1
killSwitch.reconnectFailed: Kill Switch changed, but reconnecting failed. Connect again.
mode.city.description: A city in the selected country
mode.city.label: City
mode.city.tooltip: Connects to a server in the selected city.
mode.country.description: A country code or full name
mode.country.label: Country
mode.country.tooltip: Connects to a server in the selected country.
mode.fastest.label: Fastest server
mode.fastest.tooltip: Connects to the fastest VPN server on your plan.
mode.p2p.label: P2P
mode.p2p.tooltip: Peer-to-peer servers. Required for port forwarding.
mode.paidBlocked: %1 needs a paid Proton VPN plan. Fastest server works on the free plan.
mode.random.label: Random
mode.random.tooltip: Connects to a random Proton VPN server.
mode.securecore.description: Extra Proton-owned hop before the exit
mode.securecore.label: Secure Core
mode.securecore.tooltip: Extra Proton-owned hop before the exit. Paid plans.
mode.server.description: A specific server such as CH#242
mode.server.label: Server ID
mode.server.tooltip: Connects to a specific server such as CH#242.
mode.tor.label: Tor
mode.tor.tooltip: Tor over VPN, including .onion sites. NetShield will not work.
notify.dropBlocked: Kill Switch is blocking internet traffic until the VPN reconnects.
notify.giveUpBlocked: Kill Switch is still blocking internet traffic. Open the panel to connect again.
notify.giveUpOpen: You're no longer protected. Open the panel to connect again.
notify.leakTitle: Proton VPN is not covering everything
portForwarding.active: Port forwarding is active on this server. The Proton CLI does not show the forwarded port; Proton's Linux guide reads it with natpmpc.
portForwarding.unsupported: Port forwarding is on, but this server does not support it. Connect in P2P mode to use it.
quick.activeTip: You are connected here. Press f to star or unstar it.
reconnect.disconnectAfter: Disconnecting once the current reconnect attempt finishes…
reconnect.gaveUp: Could not reconnect after the VPN dropped. Connect again.
reconnect.pending: Reconnect when the VPN drops is on; the next attempt runs shortly. Connecting or disconnecting yourself cancels it.
refresh.tipUpdated: Updated %1. Refresh status, locations, and settings (r)
routing.dnsGlobalLeak: DNS goes to %1, set system-wide, instead of the tunnel's resolver.
routing.dnsLeak: DNS goes to %1 on %2, outside the tunnel.
routing.ipv4Leak: IPv4 traffic leaves through %1, outside the tunnel.
routing.ipv6Leak: IPv6 traffic leaves through %1, outside the tunnel.
server.empty: Enter a Proton VPN server ID such as IT#23.
server.invalid: Server IDs look like IT#23 or CH-IS#1. Proton lists them in the account server list.
setting.anonymous-crash-reports.label: Anonymous Crash Reports
setting.anonymous-crash-reports.tooltip: Sends anonymous crash reports to help Proton fix bugs.
setting.custom-dns.label: Custom DNS
setting.custom-dns.tooltip: Third-party DNS instead of Proton's. Needs a new connection.
setting.ipv6.label: IPv6
setting.ipv6.tooltip: IPv6 inside the tunnel when supported. Needs a new connection.
setting.kill-switch.label: Kill Switch
setting.kill-switch.tooltip: Blocks internet if the VPN drops accidentally. CLI has Standard only.
setting.kill-switch.valueDescription.off: Internet stays available if the VPN drops.
setting.kill-switch.valueDescription.sta: Blocks all internet if the VPN drops accidentally.
setting.moderate-nat.label: Moderate NAT
setting.moderate-nat.tooltip: Allows direct P2P for gaming and WebRTC. Slightly less private.
setting.netshield.label: NetShield
setting.netshield.tooltip: Proton's DNS filtering while you are connected.
setting.netshield.valueDescription.malwa: Blocks malware, spyware, and malicious domains.
setting.port-forwarding.label: Port Forwarding
setting.port-forwarding.tooltip: Opens incoming connections. Use natpmpc to get the port.
setting.vpn-accelerator.label: VPN Accelerator
setting.vpn-accelerator.tooltip: Improves connection stability and, in some cases, speed.
setup.installHint: Opens Omarchy's installer in a terminal.
setup.signInHint: Opens a terminal; this plugin never collects a password.
signout.tip: Clears the CLI's settings; signing in again needs your password and 2FA. Favorites stay.
signout.title: Sign out
state.guiConflict: Close the Proton VPN desktop app to use the CLI.
state.signedOut: Sign in to Proton VPN from a terminal.
status.incompatible: Proton VPN status output is incompatible with this plugin.

status.unknownLine: Proton VPN reported an unknown status line.
table.incompatible: Proton VPN table output is incompatible with this plugin.

tooltip.stale: Proton VPN status may be outdated.
